questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The known student life and the cultural heritage of the country, as well as the well known academic profile of the university. Also, the weater was very nice, especially at the start,  but overall I was thrilled to experience Italy as a country more closely than simply being a tourist.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, they were easy to reach and quick to respond to any questions. They also sent out a lot of information at arrival, so all was very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Correspondances on emails and check-in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly difficult and quite expensive. I lived with another student, whom I know from back home, and we looked for housing a long time ahead and found a large apartment in the city centre, but it was expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That there is very little living on campus, but if possible, they are the cheaper options. Look for housing in good time, so you have the best options. The city centre is full of life and very lovely to walk everywhere, so no matter where, it is going to be fairly easy to stay almost anywhere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy and done in 5 minutes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had a skype-call and then I was checked in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Communication and offices. They had some "funny" opening hours, but otherwise was easy and available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I was registered for the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get as big a pre-approval as you can get beforehand, so that you can try out as many courses as possible while the semester is starting, as it can be quite difficult to know about which courses are difficult, or when they are in the schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very good. I enjoyed it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was fairly easy, but that was also after my own choosing. I also tried out some courses which were fairly rough, but choose against having them for the whole semester. I find that you can choose both easy and hard courses fairly regularly.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. There was much more of a focus on teamwork and presentations, which has not been experienced at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Fundamentals in Health Economics, Global Health Policy - Topics in Global Health, International Politics, Macroeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of these courses were good and meaningful. I would reccomend them all.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travel and stays at other cities, as well as a lot of social events which could be rather costly.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and groceries were much cheaper than back home, but rent was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you wanted to, you could be very active in social events and clubs and sports, especially through organizations like ESPN.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot. I don't think there were any "limits" to what was possible for students in comparison to UCPH, but there are less parks and less green areas, as well as limited fitness possibilities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to all the social events you can and mingle as much as possible with as many different people as possible. Especially at the start, there is so much social to do, and I would try to find the energy to do everything I can and also to talk with people outside your own nationality. There is so much lost in only talking to one country's people, and so much to learn from others.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see football matches and go to see all the cities around Italy, as well as planning as many trips as possible around. A big reccomendation to Verona, Torino, Napoli, and the Dolomites. Also, eat out as much as you can, and remember that the time is limited while you are abroad, so do it as soon as you want and go for it! Also, enjoy the beaches in the summertime.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try a lot, be open and talk to as many as possible. Go to all the events and try to mingle.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found that the Italians generally take life much more slowly and relaxed, and there is much more focus on enjoying a lot of the "simple" things. Also, there is a lower technological level than in Denmark, but this is not an issue, but more so a difference I had to get used to. They are also very proud of their history and heritage, which is really fun and exciting.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The slowness and the relaxation, and the enjoyment of the local culture and heritage. Also, the food is amazing and the pride taken in it is great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go have fun and enjoy your time. Be social, eat out, go on trips, try to talk to other nationalities and just generally do what you would like to do.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different courses and dont feel to locked in to the ones you initially selected.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going on trips and trying out the local culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding the differences in the exams and the presentations, as well as finding time for all the fun things you want to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
